subtype: Approach: rebuilding routine with small checklists [Action]
passage: After the failed semester I made the list I now call my little list. Three lines only: go to every lecture, one hour of revision, five old questions. I wrote it on a sticky note and put it on my mirror. I had tried a big schedule before and it broke by the third day, so this time I kept it small on purpose. Some days I did only the first line and felt fine. My flatmate Shankar asked to look at it once, and I felt a little shy, but I showed him. By week three the ticks made a row, and I did not want to break it. On one awful day, when the lab report ate everything, I still got two of three. — Sangeeta

qa.q: What was written on Sangeeta's sticky note?
qa.a: The note said: go to every lecture, one hour of revision, five old questions.

qa.q: How did Sangeeta feel when Shankar asked to see the list?
qa.a: Sangeeta felt a little shy, but showed the list anyway.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Sangeeta add for the weeks ahead, and why?
qa.a: Sangeeta could add a weekly review of the ticks and adjust one line, because a small list keeps the habit alive but may need changes as courses get harder.

qa.q: How might Shankar see Sangeeta's list?
qa.a: Shankar asked to look at it once, which suggests curiosity and support, and saw that the list was small enough to keep.

grounding: Shows rebuilding a routine after a failed term with a very small daily checklist that stays possible even on a bad day.
